def-gaussian-process-regression-observat:
## Definition

Let $\mathcal X$ be a set, let $m:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R$, and let
$k:\mathcal X\times\mathcal X\to\mathbb R$ be symmetric and positive
semidefinite, meaning that for every finite ordered list $t_1,\ldots,t_r$
in $\mathcal X$ and every $a\in\mathbb R^r$,
$$\sum_{i,j=1}^r a_i a_j k(t_i,t_j)\ge0.$$
For finite ordered lists $A=(a_i)_{i=1}^r$ and $B=(b_j)_{j=1}^s$ in
$\mathcal X$, define
$$K_{AB}=(k(a_i,b_j))_{i,j};$$
repeated indices are allowed.

Given a real Gaussian process $f=(f_t)_{t\in\mathcal X}$ with mean
$m(t)=\mathbb E[f_t]$ and covariance
$k(s,t)=\mathbb E[(f_s-m(s))(f_t-m(t))]$, and a nonempty finite training list
$X=(x_i)_{i=1}^n$ in $\mathcal X$, define $f_X=(f_{x_i})_{i=1}^n$ and
$m_X=(m(x_i))_{i=1}^n$. For an independent centered Gaussian noise vector
$\varepsilon\sim N_n(0,R)$ with symmetric positive-semidefinite covariance
$R$, define the observation vector $Y=f_X+\varepsilon$ and the matrix
$A_X=K_{XX}+R$.

For a nonempty finite test list $X_*=(x_j^*)_{j=1}^p$ in $\mathcal X$,
define the latent test
vector $f_*=f_{X_*}$. If a centered Gaussian vector
$\eta_*\sim N_p(0,R_*)$ with symmetric positive-semidefinite covariance
$R_*$ is independent of both $f$ and $\varepsilon$, define the noisy test
vector $Y_*=f_*+\eta_*$.
lem-finite-span-orthogonal-projection-in:
## Statement

Let $H$ be a real inner-product space and $V\subseteq H$ a finite-dimensional
subspace. For each $f\in H$ there is a unique $p\in V$ such that $f-p$ is
orthogonal to $V$, meaning $\langle f-p,v\rangle=0$ for every $v\in V$.
For every $v\in V$,
$$\|f-v\|^2=\|f-p\|^2+\|p-v\|^2.$$
In particular, $\|f\|^2=\|p\|^2+\|f-p\|^2$.
lem-gp-regression-observed-covariance-in:
## Statement

In the finite observation model, let $K=K_{XX}$ and let $R$ be symmetric and
positive semidefinite. Then $A=K+R$ is symmetric and positive semidefinite.
Its ordinary inverse exists if and only if $A$ is positive definite,
equivalently if and only if all singular values of $A$ are positive. Thus the
standard inverse formulas are defined exactly under $A\succ0$; no ordinary
inverse formula applies when $A$ is singular.
thm-gp-regression-log-marginal-likelihoo:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $\mathcal X$ be a set, let $f=(f_t)_{t\in\mathcal X}$ be a
real Gaussian process with mean $m$ and symmetric positive-semidefinite
covariance kernel $k$, and let $X=(x_i)_{i=1}^n\in\mathcal X^n$ with $n\ge1$.
For independent observation noise $\varepsilon\sim N_n(0,R)$ with symmetric
positive-semidefinite covariance $R$, set $Y=f_X+\varepsilon$,
$m_X=(m(x_i))$, $K_{XX}=(k(x_i,x_j))$, and $A_X=K_{XX}+R$. Suppose
$A_X$ is positive definite. Define the log marginal likelihood at
$y\in\mathbb R^n$ as the logarithm of the Lebesgue density of $Y$ at $y$
under this prior-predictive model. Then $Y\sim N_n(m_X,A_X)$ and
$$\log p(y\mid X,m,k,R)=-\frac12(y-m_X)^TA_X^{-1}(y-m_X)-\frac12\log\det(A_X)-\frac n2\log(2\pi).$$
This formula is asserted only for the nonsingular observed-covariance case
$A_X\succ0$.
cor-gp-regression-posterior-predictive-l:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $\mathcal X$ be a set, $m:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R$, and
$k:\mathcal X\times\mathcal X\to\mathbb R$ a symmetric kernel whose every
finite Gram quadratic form on points of $\mathcal X$ is nonnegative. Let
$f=(f_t)_{t\in\mathcal X}$ be the canonical Gaussian process with
$m(t)=\mathbb E[f_t]$ and
$k(s,t)=\mathbb E[(f_s-m(s))(f_t-m(t))]$. For finite ordered lists
$A=(a_i)_{i=1}^r$ and $B=(b_j)_{j=1}^s$ in $\mathcal X$, set
$K_{AB}=(k(a_i,b_j))$; repetitions are allowed. Take
$X=(x_i)_{i=1}^n\in\mathcal X^n$ and
$X_*=(x_j^*)_{j=1}^p\in\mathcal X^p$ with $n,p\ge1$, and write
$m_X=(m(x_i))$, $m_*=(m(x_j^*))$, $f_X=(f_{x_i})$, and
$f_*=(f_{x_j^*})$. Let $\varepsilon\sim N_n(0,R)$ be independent of $f$,
where $R$ is symmetric positive semidefinite, and set $Y=f_X+\varepsilon$ and
$A_X=K_{XX}+R$. Suppose $A_X$ is positive definite. Then for every
$y\in\mathbb R^n$ the conditional law of $f_*$ given $Y=y$ has mean
$$m_*+K_{*X}A_X^{-1}(y-m_X)$$
and covariance
$$K_{**}-K_{*X}A_X^{-1}K_{X*}.$$
This covariance is positive semidefinite and may be singular. If
$\eta_*\sim N_p(0,R_*)$ is independent of both $f$ and $\varepsilon$, where
$R_*$ is symmetric positive semidefinite, then the conditional law of
$f_*+\eta_*$ has the same mean and covariance with $R_*$ added. The displayed
kernel is defined for every $y$, although regular conditional versions are
determined only $P_Y$-almost surely.
thm-gp-regression-kernel-ridge-posterior:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $T$ be a set, let $k:T\times T\to\mathbb R$ be a symmetric
kernel whose every finite Gram quadratic form is nonnegative, and let
$m:T\to\mathbb R$. Let $H$ be a real
Hilbert space of functions on $T$ such that, for every $x\in T$, the section
$k_x:T\to\mathbb R$, $k_x(t)=k(t,x)$, belongs to $H$ and satisfies
$h(x)=\langle h,k_x\rangle_H$ for every $h\in H$. Assume $m\in H$. For a
nonempty finite ordered list $X=(x_i)_{i=1}^n$ (repetitions allowed), let
$K=K_{XX}=(k(x_i,x_j))$, $m_X=(m(x_i))$, and take $y\in\mathbb R^n$ and
$\sigma>0$. On the affine space $m+H$, define
$$J(g)=\sum_{i=1}^n(y_i-g(x_i))^2+\sigma^2\lVert g-m\rVert_H^2.$$
Then $J$ has a unique minimizer
$$g_*=m+\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i k_{x_i},\qquad \alpha=(K+\sigma^2 I_n)^{-1}(y-m_X).$$
Its evaluation vector is
$$ (g_*(x_i))_{i=1}^n=m_X+K(K+\sigma^2I_n)^{-1}(y-m_X). $$
Under AC, the mean and kernel determine a canonical cylinder-space
Gaussian-process prior. If it is observed at $X$ with independent
$N_n(0,\sigma^2I_n)$ noise, this vector is the conditional mean of the latent
evaluation vector given the observation $Y=y$. The Hilbert-space existence
and reproducing-section properties are hypotheses here; the theorem makes no
general kernel-to-Hilbert-space existence claim.
